title: RTK Query Persistence and the Loading Incident Checkpoint

questions.prompt: After process death, a raw persisted pending entry returns but no request exists. What explains the loader?

options.label: Restored execution metadata can block initiation without restoring the actual request.
Every restart automatically recreates the original fetch promise.
A pending entry proves that the server is still computing the request.

questions.explanation: Serialized pending state does not recreate a promise or prove server activity. The thunk can reject a duplicate initiation for that key even when the original client request no longer exists.

questions.prompt: Which statement about RTK 2.2.8 and 2.12.0 rehydration is accurate?

options.label: Every RTK rehydration path always restores pending entries.
Installing 2.12.0 repairs every custom persistence reconciler automatically.
Their dedicated extractRehydrationInfo reducer path filters pending entries; raw state restoration can bypass it.

questions.explanation: The inspected dedicated reducers skip pending entries in both versions. Generic state restoration is a separate path, and upgrading alone cannot guarantee the correctness of custom persistence wiring.

questions.prompt: Why filter pending records both before writing and after reading old storage?

options.label: Reading alone proves future versions never persist pending records.
Writes prevent recurrence; reads repair already persisted bad entries.
Writing alone guarantees existing disk data is immediately migrated.

questions.explanation: Both directions cover distinct populations: future snapshots and existing installations. A write filter does not itself migrate old data; a read repair does not prevent malformed snapshots from being written.

questions.prompt: The app has unsynced drafts alongside a broken API cache. What repair is preferable?

options.label: A targeted versioned cache repair that preserves unrelated durable data.
A blanket storage purge because all Redux state is disposable.
Delete the draft slice to reduce the number of cached queries.

questions.explanation: Drafts may be irreplaceable. A scoped migration can repair regenerable cache without erasing them; deleting unrelated data neither explains nor fixes the pending lifecycle defect.

questions.prompt: Which regression best proves the forever-loading repair?

options.label: Assert only that refetch was called.
Mock the query hook to return successful data.
Restore through the real config, subscribe, observe a new fake request, and reach data or error UI.

questions.explanation: The real restore and request path must progress. A refetch invocation may be blocked by the thunk, and a mocked successful hook bypasses the defect entirely.

questions.prompt: A restored pending purchase marker is removed. What follows?

options.label: Mark the purchase successful because pending implies eventual success.
Reconcile the server operation; removing local state does not justify replay.
Automatically resubmit the purchase because removal proves it never committed.

questions.explanation: The local marker cannot establish the remote outcome. Both automatic replay and assumed success can be wrong; durable command IDs and server status/idempotency are needed.
